heroHeadline: Iran Submits Formal Response to US Peace Plan — Day 71; Russia-Ukraine Ceasefire Under Strain (147 Clashes); Kevin Warsh Senate Vote This Week
heroSubtitle: On May 10, 2026 — Day 71 of the US-Iran war — Iran formally submitted its response to the US 14-point peace proposal through Pakistani intermediaries per state media agency IRNA, with contents undisclosed but Iran's position characterized as wanting a full cessation of hostilities before any nuclear talks; Qatari Prime Minister Al Thani flew to Miami to join Secretary of State Rubio, Special Envoy Witkoff, and VP Vance in a second mediation channel alongside Pakistan's, as Axios reported the US and Iran were 'closing in on a one-page memo' to end the war — with the ceasefire technically holding, 22,500 mariners still trapped on 1,550+ vessels, and Brent crude modestly easing toward ~$103–107/bbl on peace optimism. Simultaneously, Trump's brokered Russia-Ukraine 3-day ceasefire (May 9–11) was under severe strain on Day 1: Ukraine reported 147 front-line clashes and 27 Russian drones launched overnight killing 1 civilian, Russia accused Ukraine of violations, yet Putin publicly said the war was 'coming to an end' and expressed willingness to meet Zelensky after a full peace treaty — with Geneva talks set for the week of May 12 and the key sticking point being Russia's demand Ukraine withdraw from Donetsk areas Russia failed to capture. On the domestic front, Kevin Warsh's full Senate floor confirmation vote as Federal Reserve Chair is expected this week before Powell exits May 15 — confirmation near-certain with Republicans holding 53 seats plus Sen. Fetterman (D-PA) supporting — and the $72B ICE/CBP reconciliation bill is advancing toward Trump's June 1 deadline; EU-US trade negotiators met as Trump's July 4 tariff deadline for the EU approaches.
